mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for at least 3 consecutive months, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return tends to be positive due to lower borrowing costs encouraging equity investment.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < mean(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 20-day returns during high-rate regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims coinciding with a decline in wage growth (UNRATE rising while HOUST falls) predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns as investor sentiment deteriorates.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by > 0.5% while HOUST decreases over the next month
regime_hint: Labor market weakening before a recession
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive such labor-market signal events, the 20-day forward returns are not negative (median p-value > 0.5 in t-test vs. prior month).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for two consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals expanding economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO[12m moving average] for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 10 such INDPRO momentum events, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a baseline of zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly jumps above 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is negative due to market anticipation of tighter monetary policy.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.0 and CPIAUCSL[t+1] > CPIAUCSL[t] over two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 5 such CPI spikes, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during non-spike periods (median p-value > 0.5 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months, while the Federal Funds Rate remains unchanged, predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as deflationary expectations ease financing costs.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 and FEDFUNDS == FEDFUNDS[previous month] for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 4 such deflationary windows, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during stable inflation windows (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, one-time spike in job openings (PAYEMS) exceeding historical averages by at least 20% in a month is followed by a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as market participants anticipate a labor market cooling.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS[t] > PAYEMS[t-12 months] * 1.2 and PAYEMS[t-1] <= PAYEMS[t-12 months] * 1.2
failure_condition: In 10 such spikes, the 5-day forward returns are not consistently negative (median p-value > 0.5 in t-test vs. prior month).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but proxy via HOUST as a demand proxy) above the prior month's level for two months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as consumer demand strengthens.
candidate_trigger: HOUST[t] > HOUST[t-1] and HOUST[t+1] > HOUST[t] for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Early signs of consumer demand recovery
failure_condition: In 8 such demand momentum events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (median p-value > 0.5 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months, below its 12-month moving average, predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals weakening economic activity and tighter credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO[12m moving average] for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 7 such contraction episodes, the 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative (median p-value > 0.5 in t-test vs. prior regime).
